reading.body:
The insurance lines written against AI hardware name the same chokepoints the industry worries about: Taiwan fabrication, four-year grid equipment lead times, cooling failure, and packaging cleanrooms.

The ten items divide into four groups. Transit and cargo cover for GPU shipments. Geographic concentration, meaning Taiwan foundry exposure and rare earth export bottlenecks. Power and cooling equipment, meaning transformer and switchgear lead times of two to four years, precision pumps in direct to chip systems, and thermal destruction of accelerators when cooling is lost. And the physical plant itself, meaning fibre trenching delays, packaging cleanroom contamination, and custom silicon logic flaws. Only one of the ten concerns the chip as a designed object. The other nine concern moving it, powering it, cooling it, packaging it, or the materials it depends on.

That distribution is the useful signal. The risks an insurer is willing to name are the ones with enough loss history to price, and almost none of them sit inside the accelerator. They sit in the buildings and the grid around it. A two to four year lead time on transformers and switchgear is a schedule constraint on any new cluster, and it is named here as an insurable operational delay rather than a procurement problem. Cooling loss destroying accelerators, pump failure in direct to chip systems, and particulate contamination at packaging plants are all failures of the facility, not the silicon.

What this does not establish is frequency or severity. There are no premiums, limits, loss amounts, or dates of past events, and no sources are attached to any of the ten entries. It is a taxonomy of what someone believes is coverable, not evidence of what has gone wrong or how often. It also does not say which of these policies are actually written and which are only contemplated. Read it as a map of where the physical supply chain is thought to be fragile, not as a measurement of how fragile it is.

summary: Cover on the physical inputs. Cargo and transit on high value GPU shipments, foundry concentration risk in Taiwan, thermal shock damage during cooling failure, transformer and switchgear lead times running to four years, secondary market accelerator warranties, delay in startup on fibre trenching, rare earth export bottlenecks, custom silicon logic flaws, pump failures, and cleanroom contamination at packaging plants.
